sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Celtchair is an Irish hero. The Celts treated the laws of Hospitality as serious duty. Celtchair broke that tradition when he spilled blood on the Fidchell board. His king, Concobar Mac Nessa, was playing a game there against the hero Cúchulainn. To repair his damaged reputation, Celtchair took on three impossible tasks. He finished two of them. He then killed a spectral dog that had plagued the land. The dog's poisonous blood ended his life. He died with his honor intact.

okr.objective: Celtchair is the Irish hero who repaired his reputation and died with honor.
